channel.title: CIS 301 - Logical Foundations of Programming :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description: Course Description Logical formalisms used to model and reason about computer systems. Propositional and predicate logic, syntax, semantics, and proof theory; soundness and completeness issues. Mathematical induction. Program verification: invariants and program logics. Credit Hours 2 credits Course Overview This course provides an introduction to formal logic and its application to mathematical reasoning and software correctness. Students will learn to represent and analyze logical statements using propositional and predicate logic, evaluate arguments and proofs, and apply formal reasoning techniques such as equivalence laws, deduction rules, contradiction, and induction. Topics include truth tables, sets, quantifiers, logical proofs, and the translation of natural language into formal symbolic expressions. The course also examines the use of logic in computing, with an emphasis on reasoning about program correctness through specifications, preconditions, postconditions, invariants, loops, functions, and program termination. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply formal methods to analyze logical arguments and verify the correctness of computational systems.
